title: Bunny Berigan playing Stardust and Armstrong's All-American pick
summary: Randolph mistook Bunny Berigan for Armstrong; Armstrong told him he picked Berigan as his favorite trumpeter because he played Armstrong's style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I hear a lot of trumpeters, a lot of trumpeters, they're going here and going up there and ducking here -- they remind me of a fox, they're ducking in here and ducking out here. But they still haven't got the soul and the expression that that man had. That's my way of -- and I've heard many a trumpeter go play, and I haven't heard them really play with that -- you know what? I'm going to tell you something. One night, we heard a trumpet playing 'Stardust.' And oh, he was really playing. And I said, come on, come on, listen to Louis. Louis playing 'Stardust.' Louis' playing 'Stardust.' So when they finished playing, the announcer said, you just

Bunny Berigan playing Stardust. Now, I told you (unintelligible) to say this. Louis told me, Randy, the press jumped all over me when they asked me to pick my All-American trumpeter. They asked Louis to do that -- that I picked Bunny Berigan. He says, they tell me -- they say, why did you pick -- say, Bunny Berigan, Louis, says, when there was Red Allen and they called all the rest of those boys around, Red Allen and so many other trumpet players, There are numerous trumpet players, Colored trumpet players. And Louis said, you know, Randy, I picked somebody that played Louis Armstrong. He says, if I picked any of the other trumpet players, that mean that I don't like Louis Armstrong style.
That's what he told me. So there's the "I" again.
Well, I think to play that way, you really have to have a great big "I", a very big ego.
To play that grandly and really have the motivation to go out there and do something like that. You have to have a tremendous ego.
That's right. So that was one man
could really -- that was one man that could really play like Louis Armstrong. Are you acquainted with -- let's see, Bunny's dead, too, isn't he?
Oh, Bunny Berigan died around 1941, I think. I've heard most of the records.
